title: France student protests
ticker: BREAKING: More than 260,000 high school students march across France
Students protest crumbling schools, missing teachers and overcrowded classes
More than 6,000 arrested since the movement began, most of them minors
Unions demand 10 billion euros for education "right now"
Prime Minister Lecornu promises new measures by the end of the month

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Good evening, and welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: In France, more than *two hundred sixty thousand* high school students have taken to the streets.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: What began at a single school outside Paris has turned into the biggest student movement in France in *decades*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Police have arrested thousands, and some schools have been *set on fire*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Tonight: why teenagers are blockading their own schools, how it turned *violent*, and how the government is responding.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Tuesday, October sixth, students marched in cities across France.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: France's Interior Ministry counted more than *two hundred sixty thousand* high school students, including fifty six thousand in Paris.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Organizers put the total turnout even higher, at around *four hundred fifty thousand*, including teachers, parents and university students.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Twenty thousand marched in Lyon. Thirteen thousand five hundred in Toulouse. Twelve thousand five hundred in Nantes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Unlike the days before, Tuesday's marches were *largely peaceful*, often guided by parents and union members.

items.text: Teachers strike in Creteil, near Paris

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It started in *Creteil*, in the Paris suburbs.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A day after teachers went on strike over a lack of staff and resources, pupils at the Lycee Saint-Exupery organised their own protest.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Videos spread on social media, and within days, schools across the Paris suburbs were being *blockaded*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: By October first, the government said more than *a thousand high schools* were affected in a single day.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The movement has since spread across France, and even into parts of *Belgium*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So what are these students so angry about? The answer is inside their *classrooms*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Students describe classes of *thirty two to thirty five* pupils.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: When teachers leave or fall ill, they often *aren't replaced*. One student union leader cited a pupil who went seven months without a French teacher, in a year with a French exam.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Buildings are falling apart. In Saint-Denis, one protester told CBS News, ceilings are crumbling, there is water in the walls, and *rats*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: During this year's heat waves, some classrooms reached *forty degrees Celsius*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And students say *Parcoursup*, the national website used to apply to university, adds enormous stress.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: More than half of all schools are short staffed this year, according to a survey by a secondary teachers' union.

scenes.name: Rania, 15
scenes.quote: We don't feel listened to at all. We feel inferior, especially considering that we're the future.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Students told Al Jazeera they simply don't feel heard.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Rania, fifteen, said: we don't feel listened to at all. We feel *inferior*, especially considering that we're the future.

scenes.name: Olympe, 16
scenes.quote: Teachers are absent, and compared with schools in Paris we don't have the same resources.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Olympe, sixteen, pointed to *inequality*. Teachers are absent, she said, and compared with schools in Paris, we don't have the same resources.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The movement began in the suburbs of Paris, areas that have long been *underserved*.

scenes.name: Clemence, 30
scenes.quote: Their demands are ones we've been making for years.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Many teachers are marching *with* their students.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Clemence, a math teacher in Paris, said: I support the high schoolers' movement one hundred percent. *Their demands are ones we've been making for years*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A major secondary teachers' union called a *strike* in support of the students' demands.

scenes.name: Theo, 19
scenes.quote: We're really short of resources. Not just schools, but hospitals too.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For some, the anger goes beyond schools. Theo, nineteen, said: we're really *short of resources*, not just in schools, but hospitals too.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Macron's government, he said, has to *stop investing only in war*. We all have the same demands: a better future.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The protests coincide with a public sector strike over the government's *budget plans*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But in the days before Tuesday's march, the protests turned *violent*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Riot police were sent to break up school blockades, using *tear gas* and stun grenades.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: More than *six thousand* protesters have been arrested, eighty five percent of them under eighteen.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In the northern town of Lens, a fifteen year old *lost a hand* after picking up a police grenade, according to authorities.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Officials say some two hundred ten teenagers and seven hundred fifteen police officers have been wounded.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Near Paris, a fourteen year old suffered a *double fracture of the jaw* after allegedly being hit in the face by a tear gas grenade.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Some schools were *set on fire*. The education minister says twenty four have been ransacked or burned.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: France's police watchdog has opened at least *ten investigations* into police conduct, and Amnesty International has warned against excessive force.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On October second, authorities *closed more than four hundred* high schools, switching many to remote classes.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Prefects banned gatherings outside the closed schools.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin told prosecutors to seek *parental liability*, so families would pay for damage caused by their children.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The education minister said the movement had been *taken hostage* by ultra violent groups, and warned parents that in the street, children are in danger.

scenes.name: Sebastien Lecornu
scenes.quote: The government blames far-left groups. The opposition calls the movement spontaneous.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The government accuses the far left party *France Unbowed* of stirring up the unrest.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office called it an operation organised by the party and its proxies. The party says the government is *sinking into conspiracism*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In parliament, Lecornu said that *burning a high school* does not improve the state of high school buildings.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So what is the government offering the students?

items.text: Urgent teacher gaps fixed in 8 days

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On October second, the government met student leaders and announced a *five point plan* for public schools. Students called it not enough.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Student unions have united behind one demand: *ten billion euros* for education, right now.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: They say the movement will stop when the government writes that check.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The education ministry is set to receive an extra *one point two billion euros* next year, which opposition parties say barely keeps up with inflation.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Education Minister Edouard Geffray promised that all urgent teacher replacement problems would be dealt with *in eight days*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But the government ruled out scrapping *Parcoursup*, promising only to make it more transparent and simpler.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Prime Minister Lecornu has pledged new measures *by the end of the month*. A new platform for student complaints received some forty thousand submissions in its first days.

scenes.name: Emmanuel Macron
scenes.quote: Outgoing president. Presidential election next spring.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The crisis is a fresh test for outgoing President *Emmanuel Macron*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: His government is mired in political deadlock, with a *presidential election* due next spring.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: France has seen this before. In 1990, around a hundred fifty thousand high school students protested nationwide, and the government answered with an *emergency plan* and a bigger education budget.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For now, the students say they are *not backing down*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Another big march is planned for *October seventeenth*, bringing together high schoolers, university students and farmers.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: As one sixteen year old put it: if nothing changes, *we'll keep going* for much longer. Reporting for KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: To recap tonight's top story.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: More than two hundred sixty thousand French high school students marched on Tuesday, protesting *crumbling schools*, missing teachers and overcrowded classes.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: More than six thousand have been arrested, and dozens of schools damaged or burned.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Students want *ten billion euros*. The government promises fixes within weeks.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following this story. That's all for tonight. This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching, and good night.
